### LOW: Threat model T\-041 says no production RAM prefix tier exists, but the config reference documents an opt\-in resident tier forwarded to launchd
[docs/reference/configuration\.md:502](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/079c37eabd33cafd3e7925851ea3c95d76f6db44/docs/reference/configuration.md#L502) · A-001, ADV-002, T-041

The head text of configuration\.md documents \`DARKBLOOM\_PREFIX\_CACHE\_MEMORY\` \(line 502\), forwarded by LaunchAgent\. It is an explicit opt\-in for paged resident blocks and the recurrent RAM bank\. Lines 531\-532 add hybrid recurrent\-checkpoint retention through \`DARKBLOOM\_CBV2\_HYBRID\_PREFIX\_\*\`, and line 349 adds a MiMo complete\-prefix gate\. T\-041's mitigations state that production never constructs or funds a resident\-RAM prefix cache and that there is no production RAM tier or tier composition\. T\-041 also describes the SSD tier as default\-on for every eligible CBv2 model, whereas line 501 says the default is on only for exact cohorts\. A provider operator who sets the memory opt\-in gets a shared\-across\-tenants resident cache\. It carries the same TTFT hit/miss oracle \(SEC\-035, leak \#1\) with no TTL, no HMAC\-keyed names and no at\-rest encryption story\. Those controls are only analysed for the SSD tier\. I could not see the diff, so I cannot say whether this tier was introduced by this PR\. Fix: update T\-041 to cover the opt\-in resident tier\. State its salt scoping and lifetime, whether in\-memory data is cleared on unload, and the exact default\-on cohort\. Or correct the docs if the tier is not reachable in production\.
